profiles.meeting_scenario: A troubleshooting meeting at a university software engineering lab about a prototype for simulated interactive debugging used in an introductory programming course. During a pilot run the previous afternoon, several students reported that after the first execution of their code, the tool's automated breakpoint guidance and chat assistant appeared to hang or stop updating. The meeting is between the backend engineer responsible for the orchestration service that combines fault localization with an LLM, and the course tools engineer who maintains the browser/IDE integration used by students. The agenda is to compare observed symptoms, identify the most likely root cause before the next day's lab section, and agree on a low-risk fix plus a validation plan. The expected outcome is a shared plan for what to patch today and how they will verify that the issue is resolved in time for the next class.

members.name: Priya Natarajan
members.expertise: Distributed application services, observability, request orchestration, LLM-backed developer tools
members.background: Priya built the prototype's guidance orchestrator that coordinates fault localization, breakpoint suggestion generation, and chat responses across containerized services running in Kubernetes.
members.private_state: Priya wants the fastest safe mitigation before tomorrow's lab and is quietly worried that the recent inference-service rollout may be causing session state loss; she prefers a backend-side patch that avoids touching student-facing tooling right before class.
hidden_assumptions: When people say a 'session', they mean the live backend debugging session keyed by the current websocket connection and run ID.
A 'staging replay' is valid if it replays API traffic against staging services, even without the actual student browser extension in the loop.
The issue is 'fixed' once the orchestrator no longer drops state and synthetic runs complete without timeout or repeated error logs.
The 'latest rollout' relevant to this bug is Friday evening's inference-service container update.
If they need to 'capture a trace', the useful trace is server-side correlation IDs, debug logs, and spans across the orchestrator and inference services.

members.name: Lucas Meyer
members.expertise: IDE and browser integrations, LMS tooling, student workflow instrumentation, educational developer experience
members.background: Lucas maintains the VS Code plugin and web integration that students use to launch guided debugging sessions from course assignments and has been collecting pilot feedback from TAs and students.
members.private_state: Lucas wants to prevent another visibly broken student experience during tomorrow's lab and is privately concerned that the newest client plugin update may be mishandling reconnects; he prefers verification that mirrors an actual student workflow, not just backend health.
hidden_assumptions: When people say a 'session', they mean one student's debugging attempt for an assignment, even if the browser tab reconnects or the plugin restarts in the middle.
A 'staging replay' only counts if it uses the test course, real assignment submissions, and the same plugin flow students trigger from the UI.
The issue is 'fixed' only if a student can complete a full run-breakpoint-chat-rerun cycle without manually refreshing or reopening the tool.
The 'latest rollout' relevant to this bug is Monday morning's automatic plugin update for the course tools.
If they need to 'capture a trace', the useful trace is a client-side event timeline with plugin logs, websocket reconnects, and UI state transitions.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the same debugging session
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both talk about 'the session getting stuck after the first run.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the backend websocket-scoped execution session associated with a single live run ID; if the client reconnects, that is effectively a new session.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the student's overall debugging attempt for one assignment problem, including reconnects, reruns, and UI recovery within the same work period.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In normal troubleshooting talk, 'session' sounds like an obvious shared term, and both are discussing the same visible symptom, so neither notices that one is grouping multiple reconnects together while the other is not.

misalignment_points.topic: Which recent update they are blaming
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to 'the latest rollout' or 'the recent update' as the likely change that introduced the issue.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the Friday inference-service container rollout that changed request streaming and cache handling.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the Monday plugin auto-update that changed how the client re-attaches after a code run completes.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both updates happened recently and both are genuinely plausible contributors, so 'latest rollout' feels specific enough in context even though they are mentally pointing to different artifacts.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to verify the fix in staging
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that 'if it passes in staging, we can ship the fix for tomorrow's lab.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks passing means synthetic request replays through staging show no state-loss errors, successful breakpoint suggestions, and clean orchestrator traces for at least several runs.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks passing means a TA can open the test course, launch the tool from the UI, run code twice, chat once, and see guidance continue without any manual refresh.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using the same operational phrase about staging verification, and each criterion sounds like a reasonable version of 'passes,' so the distinction stays hidden unless someone explicitly asks for the acceptance procedure.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'capture a trace on the next reproduction.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 plans to enable backend debug logging and trace spans using correlation IDs across the orchestrator and inference service.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 plans to collect plugin logs, websocket reconnect events, and a HAR file from the browser-based debugging UI.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In engineering meetings, 'get a trace' is common shorthand and usually sounds like a minor implementation detail, so neither party expects it to require clarification.
